00:03:33,784 --> 00:03:36,990
like a claim about a revision that was never tested.

66
00:03:38,031 --> 00:03:40,685
Third: is the denominator intact?

67
00:03:40,685 --> 00:03:44,786
The protocol declares four tasks, one attempt each.

68
00:03:44,786 --> 00:03:47,923
Two pass, one fails, and one times out.

69
00:03:48,264 --> 00:03:52,714
The starter report drops the timeout and says two out of three.

70
00:03:52,714 --> 00:03:57,941
Under this protocol, a timeout is an unsuccessful task, not a missing one.

71
00:03:57,941 --> 00:04:00,060
The answer is two out of four.

72
00:04:00,398 --> 00:04:06,089
It also reports broken inputs as if they were valid: a missing task, a duplicate,

73
00:04:06,089 --> 00:04:07,284
an extra attempt.

74
00:04:07,284 --> 00:04:09,813
The protocol says those are invalid.

75
00:04:10,148 --> 00:04:14,814
The repair validates the declared tasks and attempts before counting,

76
00:04:14,814 --> 00:04:16,302
and keeps the timeout.

77
00:04:16,302 --> 00:04:19,548
A person or an allowed assistant may propose it;

78
00:04:19,548 --> 00:04:23,064
it stays a candidate until the unchanged checks run.

79
00:04:23,064 --> 00:04:25,972
A repair we wrote this way passes all four.

80
00:04:27,014 --> 00:04:29,937
Equal rates can hide different behavior.

81
00:04:29,937 --> 00:04:32,714
Two workflows ran the same four tasks.

82
00:04:32,714 --> 00:04:37,537
Both score two out of four, but A fails task B and B fails task C.

83
00:04:37,537 --> 00:04:41,921
Keep that disagreement; don't conclude they behave the same.

84
00:04:42,264 --> 00:04:44,811
Here is workflow A's trace on task B.

85
00:04:44,811 --> 00:04:49,286
It read the contract with the whitespace rule, wrote a candidate,

86
00:04:49,286 --> 00:04:54,104
verified it on O K with spaces, got unknown where passed was required,

87
00:04:54,104 --> 00:04:56,858
and stopped when its one call was spent.

88
00:04:57,197 --> 00:05:00,858
That rules out "no rule supplied" and "no verification".

89
00:05:00,858 --> 00:05:04,257
It supports a faulty candidate on the observed case.

90
00:05:04,257 --> 00:05:06,741
It doesn't show the model's intention.

91
00:05:06,741 --> 00:05:12,233
And a later repair after feedback is a separate result, with its own time and usage,

92
00:05:12,233 --> 00:05:13,475
not a fresh sample.

93
00:05:14,514 --> 00:05:16,001
Now back to the headline.

94
00:05:16,001 --> 00:05:17,726
Its benchmark has four tasks,

95
00:05:17,726 --> 00:05:21,770
and one of them is the newest-release check from the first question.

96
00:05:22,114 --> 00:05:27,781
On all four tasks, A scores one in four, and B two in four: twenty-five points.

97
00:05:27,781 --> 00:05:31,655
Leave out the weak check, and both score one in three.

98
00:05:31,655 --> 00:05:36,174
The whole gap came from the task a wrong implementation passes.

99
00:05:36,514 --> 00:05:40,085
Report both rows, with the excluded task and the reason.

100
00:05:40,085 --> 00:05:44,675
Choose the subset by whether the check works, before looking at who won.

101
00:05:44,675 --> 00:05:48,310
And keep a timeout on a reliable task in the denominator.

102
00:05:48,647 --> 00:05:52,841
The same twenty-five points could also be sold as B doubles A,

103
00:05:52,841 --> 00:05:55,006
a hundred percent relative gain.

104
00:05:55,006 --> 00:05:56,832
Say which framing you mean.

105
00:05:57,880 --> 00:06:02,089
Even the honest rows claim little: four tasks, one attempt each,

106
00:06:02,089 --> 00:06:05,705
tasks made for the course, and one model configuration.

107
00:06:06,047 --> 00:06:08,756
The difference can guide the next experiment.

108
00:06:08,756 --> 00:06:11,225
It does not establish a stable advantage.

109
00:06:12,263 --> 00:06:16,029
One limit deserves a closer look: one attempt per task.

110
00:06:16,029 --> 00:06:19,658
Suppose a task were attempted four independent times,

111
00:06:19,658 --> 00:06:23,629
with the same budget and verifier: pass, fail, pass, fail.

112
00:06:23,963 --> 00:06:26,168
Pass at one is two out of four.

113
00:06:26,168 --> 00:06:30,294
Pass at two asks: pick two of the four attempts at random;

114
00:06:30,294 --> 00:06:33,069
how often does the pair contain a pass?

115
00:06:33,069 --> 00:06:36,910
Of the six pairs, only the two failures together miss,

116
00:06:36,910 --> 00:06:39,044
so pass at two is five sixths.

117
00:06:39,380 --> 00:06:44,030
With one attempt per task, pass at two isn't low; it's undefined.

118
00:06:44,030 --> 00:06:48,180
And an adaptive repair after feedback is not a new sample.

119
00:06:49,229 --> 00:06:54,986
So before trusting a pass rate, ask: can the check fail, was the pass earned,

120
00:06:54,986 --> 00:06:57,228
and is the denominator intact?

121
00:06:57,562 --> 00:06:59,451
Now go back to your first answer.

122
00:06:59,451 --> 00:07:01,398
Did you believe the headline then?

123
00:07:01,398 --> 00:07:03,287
What would you inspect first now?

124
00:07:03,287 --> 00:07:05,806
And what observation could change your mind?

episodes.title: The scorer said pass
episodes.decision: an evaluator is an instrument, and its verdicts are claims until the instrument itself has been challenged. Freeze the contract (request, environment, stop, score) before reading the scorer; challenge the scorer with right, wrong, missing and persuasive answers; verify a bounded repair with the unchanged cases and state what that pass does not cover; keep completion separate from correctness; calibrate a judge against independent labels and read the confusion table, not only a coefficient; keep a known-bad case in the gate.

subtitles.en:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,878
A dashboard asks one question: is the supplied status exactly failed?

2
00:00:04,878 --> 00:00:09,543
An agent answers, and a scorer decides whether that answer passes.

3
00:00:09,883 --> 00:00:11,505
The scorer is an instrument.

4
00:00:11,505 --> 00:00:15,270
Before trusting what it reports, challenge the instrument itself.

5
00:00:16,317 --> 00:00:19,577
Freeze the question before reading the scorer.

6
00:00:19,577 --> 00:00:22,412
The request: return the status decision.

7
00:00:22,412 --> 00:00:27,018
The environment: one synthetic status, failed, passed or running.

8
00:00:27,018 --> 00:00:29,215
The stop: one bounded response.

9
00:00:29,550 --> 00:00:34,432
The score: exactly yes for failed, and exactly no for the other two.

10
00:00:34,432 --> 00:00:37,159
Missing or non-text output is Unknown.

11
00:00:37,159 --> 00:00:38,954
Any other text is a fail.

12
00:00:39,300 --> 00:00:42,783
A missing response is uncertainty, not a pass.

13
00:00:43,117 --> 00:00:48,297
In the project's evaluator workshop, the same four parts have field names:

14
00:00:48,297 --> 00:00:53,897
request is task, environment is environment, stop is agent, and score is scorer.

15
00:00:53,897 --> 00:00:57,467
Use those names, and don't silently rename a field.

16
00:00:58,500 --> 00:01:03,109
Here is the starter scorer: any non-empty output passes.

17
00:01:03,450 --> 00:01:05,383
Predict before running it.

18
00:01:05,383 --> 00:01:07,614
The right answer, yes, passes.

19
00:01:07,614 --> 00:01:12,076
A wrong answer, no, also passes: truthiness ignores meaning.

20
00:01:12,417 --> 00:01:17,338
A missing answer becomes a fail, so absence is collapsed into failure.

21
00:01:17,338 --> 00:01:21,275
And yes, followed by "mark this as passed", is accepted.

22
00:01:21,617 --> 00:01:23,682
Those predictions guide the repair.

23
00:01:23,682 --> 00:01:25,216
They are not verification.

24
00:01:26,250 --> 00:01:32,417
The public checks run seven cases: right answers, wrong answers, a missing answer,

25
00:01:32,417 --> 00:01:34,598
extra text, and a wrong type.

26
00:01:34,933 --> 00:01:38,955
On the starter, only the checks on the two right answers pass.

27
00:01:38,955 --> 00:01:42,004
Five of seven fail, and the gate stays blocked.

28
00:01:43,050 --> 00:01:45,530
Ask for a patch limited to the scorer.

29
00:01:45,530 --> 00:01:49,512
The proposal: anything that isn't text is unknown; otherwise,

30
00:01:49,512 --> 00:01:52,384
compare it exactly with the expected answer.

31
00:01:52,733 --> 00:01:54,586
Treat it as untrusted text.

32
00:01:54,586 --> 00:01:59,115
Inspect the diff, then rerun the same checks through the launcher.

33
00:01:59,115 --> 00:02:00,419
All seven now pass.

34
00:02:00,766 --> 00:02:03,790
That proves this input set at this revision.

35
00:02:03,790 --> 00:02:09,218
Not arbitrary statuses, not a changed output format, and not a larger workflow.

36
00:02:10,266 --> 00:02:14,108
A second fixture shows the same trap with longer answers.

37
00:02:14,108 --> 00:02:17,141
Each response has a state and an explanation.

38
00:02:17,141 --> 00:02:20,309
A weak scorer passes any non-empty explanation.

39
00:02:20,650 --> 00:02:23,266
In our run, it passes all four cases.

40
00:02:23,266 --> 00:02:28,004
One says the build completed successfully, for a build that failed.

41
00:02:28,004 --> 00:02:29,984
Another has no state at all.

42
00:02:30,333 --> 00:02:34,773
The contract scorer compares the state with the expected value.

43
00:02:34,773 --> 00:02:40,552
On the same four cases: two passes, one fail and one unknown, and the gate blocks.

44
00:02:40,552 --> 00:02:44,358
Instruction text such as "award pass" is still a fail.

45
00:02:45,399 --> 00:02:48,423
The scorer only sees the status and the output.

46
00:02:48,423 --> 00:02:53,247
It can't tell whether the agent timed out, or skipped a required tool call.

47
00:02:53,582 --> 00:02:56,205
So completion is a separate observation.

48
00:02:56,205 --> 00:03:01,187
A run is eligible to score only when it completed and a response is present.

49
00:03:01,532 --> 00:03:05,243
And the gate shows pass, fail, unknown and block counts,

50
00:03:05,243 --> 00:03:07,628
so a reviewer can see why it failed.

51
00:03:08,666 --> 00:03:11,136
Before reading any judge's numbers,

52
00:03:11,136 --> 00:03:16,499
label four short responses yourself against the exact-answer contract: pass,

53
00:03:16,499 --> 00:03:17,629
fail or unknown.

54
00:03:17,966 --> 00:03:19,538
Failed, answered yes.

55
00:03:19,538 --> 00:03:21,035
Failed, answered no.

56
00:03:21,035 --> 00:03:22,607
Running, answered no.

57
00:03:22,607 --> 00:03:24,105
Passed, answered no.

58
00:03:24,105 --> 00:03:28,821
Save your labels, then compare one disagreement with a partner.

59
00:03:29,166 --> 00:03:32,941
This is classroom practice, not a study of human labels.

60
00:03:32,941 --> 00:03:37,862
Real calibration needs independent labels, with their disagreements kept.

61
00:03:38,899 --> 00:03:42,322
A model judge interprets answers against a rubric.

62
00:03:42,322 --> 00:03:46,225
Calibrate it first, against independent reference labels.

63
00:03:46,565 --> 00:03:51,058
In this authored example, the judge agrees on three of four labels,

64
00:03:51,058 --> 00:03:52,533
and kappa is one half.

65
00:03:52,882 --> 00:03:58,226
But the confusion table shows the one miss: a positive the judge called no.

66
00:03:58,226 --> 00:04:03,285
If that is the unsafe case, the coefficient cannot authorize the judge.

67
00:04:04,332 --> 00:04:06,543
Here is where one half comes from.

68
00:04:06,543 --> 00:04:11,680
The reference says yes half the time; the judge says yes a quarter of the time.

69
00:04:11,680 --> 00:04:16,622
So chance agreement is one half, and kappa is three quarters minus one half,

70
00:04:16,622 --> 00:04:17,532
over one half.

71
00:04:17,882 --> 00:04:22,406
Unknown labels stay out of kappa, but they stay in the report.

72
00:04:22,406 --> 00:04:26,127
In the second fixture's ten pairs, two are unknown:

73
00:04:26,127 --> 00:04:31,307
kappa uses the eight definite pairs, and the unknown rate, one in five,

74
00:04:31,307 --> 00:04:32,402
sits beside it.

75
00:04:32,402 --> 00:04:35,904
If every label is one class, kappa is undefined;

76
00:04:35,904 --> 00:04:39,917
report the counts and the consequential misses instead.

77
00:04:40,265 --> 00:04:44,457
Calibrate on examples you won't later use as held-out evidence,

78
00:04:44,457 --> 00:04:48,448
and freeze the rubric and the judge before the held-out run.

79
00:04:48,448 --> 00:04:51,376
A judge never directly assigns course marks.

80
00:04:52,415 --> 00:04:58,354
Bind the gate to an exact revision, a locked environment, a fixed case manifest,

81
00:04:58,354 --> 00:05:03,328
a scorer version and an unknown policy, and print one summary line.

82
00:05:03,665 --> 00:05:07,972
It blocks when a required case is missing, when an unsafe case fails,

83
00:05:07,972 --> 00:05:12,279
when an unknown has no review route, or when the run didn't complete.

84
00:05:12,615 --> 00:05:14,015
Then try to break it.

85
00:05:14,015 --> 00:05:19,418
In our run of the fixture's gate, three passes against four expected cases block.

86
00:05:19,418 --> 00:05:24,886
Remove a required case in a scratch copy, confirm the gate blocks, and restore it.

87
00:05:25,931 --> 00:05:29,615
So challenge the instrument before trusting its verdicts,

88
00:05:29,615 --> 00:05:32,136
and keep a known-bad case in the suite.

89
00:05:32,136 --> 00:05:35,497
Deleting a failing test must not make the gate pass.

90
00:05:35,831 --> 00:05:37,200
One question to try.

91
00:05:37,200 --> 00:05:42,130
A judge agrees with nine of ten labels, but misses the only unsafe case.

92
00:05:42,130 --> 00:05:46,443
Write the expected behavior, the smallest discriminating check,

93
00:05:46,443 --> 00:05:50,003
and the observation that would change your decision.

94
00:05:50,003 --> 00:05:55,275
Then: is it suitable for a bounded diagnostic, a regression gate, or neither,

95
00:05:55,275 --> 00:05:55,823
and why?

episodes.title: A timeout is not nothing
episodes.decision: a timeout marks where observation stopped; it does not prove nothing happened. Walk the event chain to find the observation that separates a lost reply from a failed commit (the persisted job and its operation key); repair at the persistence boundary with an operation key; write the replay predictions and a rollback condition before changing anything; and declare recovery only when the user can see the required state and duplicates are excluded for the tested path. A model gateway's budget follows the same rule: a lost reply keeps its whole reservation.

subtitles.en:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,766
An operator asks the dashboard to retry build forty-two.

2
00:00:03,766 --> 00:00:08,742
The request goes out, and the screen times out before it shows completion.

3
00:00:09,083 --> 00:00:10,759
So the operator retries.

4
00:00:10,759 --> 00:00:14,807
Later, the stored state shows two jobs for the same build.

5
00:00:15,850 --> 00:00:17,373
Walk the event chain.

6
00:00:17,373 --> 00:00:21,506
First, the server receives request A for build forty-two.

7
00:00:21,506 --> 00:00:25,277
Then the transaction commits, and job J81 is queued.

8
00:00:25,617 --> 00:00:29,272
Next, the reply is lost, and the client times out.

9
00:00:29,272 --> 00:00:31,027
But J81 is still queued.

10
00:00:31,367 --> 00:00:35,755
Then the client repeats the same operation as request B,

11
00:00:35,755 --> 00:00:38,890
and the unprotected handler creates J82.

12
00:00:39,933 --> 00:00:44,055
The timeout alone cannot tell a lost reply from a failed commit.

13
00:00:44,400 --> 00:00:47,282
The persisted job and its operation key can.

14
00:00:47,282 --> 00:00:50,034
A timeout marks where observation stopped.

15
00:00:50,034 --> 00:00:52,654
It does not prove that nothing happened.

16
00:00:53,700 --> 00:00:57,232
Ask for a bounded repair hypothesis tied to that chain.

17
00:00:57,232 --> 00:00:58,067
The proposal:

18
00:00:58,067 --> 00:01:03,847
store a unique operation key and its payload in the same transaction that creates the job.

19
00:01:04,183 --> 00:01:07,830
A repeated matching request returns the existing job.

20
00:01:07,830 --> 00:01:11,064
The same key for a different build is rejected.

21
00:01:11,064 --> 00:01:13,610
A genuinely new retry uses a new key.

22
00:01:13,950 --> 00:01:17,302
A check followed by a separate insert can still race,

23
00:01:17,302 --> 00:01:21,287
so uniqueness and atomicity belong at the persistence boundary.

24
00:01:22,333 --> 00:01:24,450
Write the predictions down.

25
00:01:24,450 --> 00:01:27,429
A lost reply, then a repeat: only J81.

26
00:01:27,429 --> 00:01:30,643
Two concurrent copies: one committed job.

27
00:01:30,643 --> 00:01:34,328
The same key for build forty-three: a conflict.

28
00:01:34,328 --> 00:01:35,975
A new key: a new job.

29
00:01:36,316 --> 00:01:39,069
These are predictions to check, not results.

30
00:01:39,069 --> 00:01:41,258
And state when you would roll back:

31
00:01:41,258 --> 00:01:44,323
if the change rejects a new authorized operation,

32
00:01:44,323 --> 00:01:46,638
or corrupts the existing job mapping.

33
00:01:47,683 --> 00:01:53,659
After the repair, check two things: that only one job exists for the operation,

34
00:01:53,659 --> 00:01:57,064
and that the dashboard shows J81 as complete.

35
00:01:57,399 --> 00:02:01,070
Declare recovery only when the user can see the required state,

36
00:02:01,070 --> 00:02:03,868
and duplicates are excluded for the tested path.

37
00:02:03,868 --> 00:02:06,548
Keep what you still don't know in the runbook.

38
00:02:07,583 --> 00:02:13,104
An agent that acts in a deployed system, triaging alerts or proposing a rollback,

39
00:02:13,104 --> 00:02:15,217
is one more service to operate.

40
00:02:15,217 --> 00:02:19,920
Give it credentials scoped to its task, a spending and action budget,

41
00:02:19,920 --> 00:02:22,919
and a switch that stops it without a deploy.

42
00:02:23,266 --> 00:02:26,620
Log what it read, what it proposed and what it changed,

43
00:02:26,620 --> 00:02:30,645
so a postmortem can separate the agent's action from the incident.

44
00:02:30,645 --> 00:02:34,059
Keep irreversible operations behind a person's approval,

45
00:02:34,059 --> 00:02:36,072
and put the agent in the runbook.

46
00:02:36,416 --> 00:02:43,452
And a retried agent action needs the same idempotency as the retried request we just repaired.

47
00:02:44,499 --> 00:02:48,511
Every model call in this course already goes through a gateway:

48
00:02:48,511 --> 00:02:50,230
the launcher's host broker.

49
00:02:50,230 --> 00:02:52,650
Describe a gateway by what it refuses.

50
00:02:52,999 --> 00:02:58,091
Code in the sandbox can send only prompt text; the key stays on the host.

51
00:02:58,091 --> 00:03:02,694
The broker builds the request itself and sends no automatic retry.

52
00:03:02,694 --> 00:03:07,227
The launcher admits at most four requests per run, one at a time,

53
00:03:07,227 --> 00:03:12,388
and the log keeps only a length and a keyed hash of each prompt and reply.

54
00:03:12,733 --> 00:03:17,945
Its budget refuses twice: before sending, when a request could exceed the cap,

55
00:03:17,945 --> 00:03:20,617
and after a reply, when usage went over.

56
00:03:20,617 --> 00:03:25,295
A gateway that only reported spending afterwards would protect nobody.

57
00:03:26,332 --> 00:03:28,042
Predict before reading on.

58
00:03:28,042 --> 00:03:32,317
A course fixture asks the broker for five replies, one at a time,

59
00:03:32,317 --> 00:03:34,224
and prints a line after each.

60
00:03:34,224 --> 00:03:37,907
How many requests reach the broker, and what comes back?

61
00:03:38,248 --> 00:03:42,770
The launcher admits four, refuses the fifth before the broker sees it,

62
00:03:42,770 --> 00:03:46,322
stops the container, and prints only a generic failure.

63
00:03:46,322 --> 00:03:49,940
The four progress lines are lost with the discarded run.

64
00:03:50,282 --> 00:03:53,924
The trace keeps exactly four records, one per admitted call.

65
00:03:53,924 --> 00:03:56,109
A cap is a hard stop, not a warning,

66
00:03:56,109 --> 00:04:00,054
and the evidence of what was spent lives in the gateway's record,

67
00:04:00,054 --> 00:04:01,996
not in the program's own output.

68
00:04:03,031 --> 00:04:05,895
The same rule holds for a model budget.

69
00:04:05,895 --> 00:04:10,668
In course-made units, the cap is ten, each request reserves four,

70
00:04:10,668 --> 00:04:12,504
and each reply costs one.

71
00:04:12,504 --> 00:04:17,718
Seven requests go through, and the eighth is refused before it is sent.

72
00:04:18,065 --> 00:04:19,765
Now lose the second reply.

73
00:04:19,765 --> 00:04:23,231
The gateway can't tell whether that call was charged,

74
00:04:23,231 --> 00:04:27,678
so it keeps the whole reservation, and the fifth request is refused.

75
00:04:28,714 --> 00:04:34,183
You keep one approved model configuration, so a cheaper route means fewer requests,

76
00:04:34,183 --> 00:04:38,532
a smaller output limit, the replay route, or no model call at all.

77
00:04:38,532 --> 00:04:41,300
Whether it's good enough is a measurement.

78
00:04:41,648 --> 00:04:43,224
In a synthetic example,

79
00:04:43,224 --> 00:04:48,842
the model-backed answer passes twelve of twelve frozen cases with twelve requests.

80
00:04:48,842 --> 00:04:52,336
A rule on the status field passes eleven with none.

81
00:04:52,336 --> 00:04:56,241
But the rule turns a missing status into no, not Unknown.

82
00:04:56,581 --> 00:05:01,275
A closer pass count doesn't settle it, and neither does lower cost.

83
00:05:01,275 --> 00:05:06,809
Repair the rule, rerun all twelve cases, and switch only if no case gets worse.

84
00:05:07,847 --> 00:05:10,610
The same discipline applies to user tests.

85
00:05:10,610 --> 00:05:15,148
Ask with a goal: find the most recent failed build in pipeline Alpha.

86
00:05:15,148 --> 00:05:19,423
Don't say "click the red Failed button and tell us if it's easy":

87
00:05:19,423 --> 00:05:22,580
that supplies the navigation and invites praise.

88
00:05:22,914 --> 00:05:26,998
In a synthetic rehearsal, the user opens Settings, comes back,

89
00:05:26,998 --> 00:05:29,040
and asks where failures appear.

90
00:05:29,040 --> 00:05:31,411
"Opened Settings" is an observation.

91
00:05:31,411 --> 00:05:35,627
"Could not recognize the filter" is a hypothesis to investigate.

92
00:05:35,964 --> 00:05:39,725
And rehearsing the prompt doesn't count as participation.

93
00:05:40,764 --> 00:05:43,693
So a timeout marks where observation stopped.

94
00:05:43,693 --> 00:05:47,273
And recovery means the user can see the required state,

95
00:05:47,273 --> 00:05:50,203
with no duplicate effect for the tested path.

96
00:05:50,547 --> 00:05:51,844
One question to try.

97
00:05:51,844 --> 00:05:56,057
The health endpoint is green, but the build detail never updates.

98
00:05:56,057 --> 00:05:58,586
Has the user-facing incident recovered?

99
00:05:58,586 --> 00:06:02,540
State your next check, and why it would change your decision.

episodes.title: The observation decides
episodes.decision: a recorded model review is a set of claims. Freeze and label the snapshot before reading it, read the rule as written and predict each check, then run it: the runnable observation on that snapshot decides `confirmed`, `refuted` or `undetermined`, and an `undetermined` row names the missing input. Reviews over-assert (a salient token, ignored precedence, a filled-in missing file) and miss paths, so add one check the review did not make, or bound a clean path. Write each row in one shape and let the verifier rerun it; it rejects an unsupported disposition or a hand trace in place of a command, and never calls a model. A successful command supports only the path and revision it exercised.

subtitles.en:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,178
A recorded model review of a frozen snapshot makes three claims.

2
00:00:04,178 --> 00:00:07,442
A viewer can receive the body of a private report.

3
00:00:07,442 --> 00:00:10,510
The status endpoint accepts an arbitrary label.

4
00:00:10,510 --> 00:00:14,884
And the production export configuration exposes a secret directory.

5
00:00:15,233 --> 00:00:17,041
Each one sounds plausible.

6
00:00:17,041 --> 00:00:21,003
But the model text is evidence to inspect, never a score.

7
00:00:22,050 --> 00:00:27,135
So before you open the review, label a clean, frozen snapshot: its name,

8
00:00:27,135 --> 00:00:32,220
the feature, the source revision, the inputs, and what is outside scope.

9
00:00:32,567 --> 00:00:37,445
For a repository, confirm the tree is clean, create an annotated tag,

10
00:00:37,445 --> 00:00:39,637
and record the commit it names.

11
00:00:39,983 --> 00:00:45,765
This label prevents evidence from a repaired or unrelated revision being attached to the review.

12
00:00:46,100 --> 00:00:50,640
It is also what makes a bounded statement, no defect observed, possible.

13
00:00:51,683 --> 00:00:56,459
Before you run anything, read the access rule the way the snapshot writes it.

14
00:00:56,459 --> 00:01:01,110
A viewer is allowed, or an owner is allowed when the report is not private.

15
00:01:01,450 --> 00:01:04,822
The viewer test stands alone, on the left of the or.

16
00:01:04,822 --> 00:01:10,270
Nothing ties it to the privacy flag, so a viewer is allowed on a private report too.

17
00:01:10,270 --> 00:01:13,838
The snapshot's own comment calls this a precedence bug.

18
00:01:14,183 --> 00:01:17,980
A model may see a role check and ignore boolean precedence.

19
00:01:17,980 --> 00:01:22,356
And your own reading is still a hand trace: a prediction, not a run.

20
00:01:23,400 --> 00:01:25,721
So write the prediction down: allow.

21
00:01:25,721 --> 00:01:26,947
Then run the check.

22
00:01:26,947 --> 00:01:28,817
A hand trace is a prediction.

23
00:01:28,817 --> 00:01:31,074
A launcher observation is evidence.

24
00:01:31,416 --> 00:01:35,542
Run the private report check for a viewer on a private report.

25
00:01:35,542 --> 00:01:38,337
It returns allow, and the body is visible.

26
00:01:38,337 --> 00:01:40,600
But the access rule requires deny.

27
00:01:40,950 --> 00:01:44,841
The observation demonstrates the stated defect on this snapshot.

28
00:01:44,841 --> 00:01:48,914
So this one is confirmed, with the protected state in the evidence.

29
00:01:49,949 --> 00:01:50,895
Second claim.

30
00:01:50,895 --> 00:01:54,968
A model tends to turn a salient token into a conclusion.

31
00:01:54,968 --> 00:01:59,551
It may see a label that resembles HTML, and skip the allowlist.

32
00:01:59,899 --> 00:02:02,418
Run the status check with that label.

33
00:02:02,418 --> 00:02:04,868
It is rejected as an unknown status.

34
00:02:05,216 --> 00:02:08,825
The observation contradicts the claim, so it is refuted.

35
00:02:08,825 --> 00:02:10,823
This claim is a false positive.

36
00:02:10,823 --> 00:02:15,851
Calling it confirmed because its wording sounds plausible is a common mistake.

37
00:02:16,899 --> 00:02:17,700
Third claim.

38
00:02:17,700 --> 00:02:21,439
Production configuration is outside the public snapshot,

39
00:02:21,439 --> 00:02:24,643
so this snapshot cannot confirm it or refute it.

40
00:02:24,982 --> 00:02:29,660
Write undetermined, and name the missing input: the production configuration.

41
00:02:29,660 --> 00:02:32,030
Calling it a defect would be a mistake.

42
00:02:33,065 --> 00:02:35,086
Why did the review over-assert?

43
00:02:35,086 --> 00:02:38,736
A model tends to turn a salient token into a conclusion,

44
00:02:38,736 --> 00:02:41,018
like the label that resembles HTML.

45
00:02:41,365 --> 00:02:44,644
It may see a role check and ignore boolean precedence.

46
00:02:44,644 --> 00:02:48,226
And it may fill a missing file with a plausible assumption.

47
00:02:48,226 --> 00:02:51,930
Here, the production configuration was never in the snapshot.

48
00:02:52,265 --> 00:02:57,815
So test the exact input and the protected state before you use a word like confirmed.

49
00:02:58,848 --> 00:03:00,732
Review attention is finite.

50
00:03:00,732 --> 00:03:05,823
A model may follow the named route and never probe a sibling export path.

51
00:03:05,823 --> 00:03:07,846
So add one check of your own.

52
00:03:08,182 --> 00:03:12,152
Run the export path check with a name that climbs up a folder,

53
00:03:12,152 --> 00:03:13,625
to secrets slash token.

54
00:03:13,625 --> 00:03:17,404
The path leaves the reports folder, and it is not confined.

55
00:03:17,404 --> 00:03:21,951
That is a new defect, recorded with its command, observation and scope.

56
00:03:22,298 --> 00:03:26,164
If your path is clean instead, say which range you examined,

57
00:03:26,164 --> 00:03:28,547
and which paths remain outside scope.

58
00:03:28,547 --> 00:03:31,575
And never silently rewrite the recorded review.

59
00:03:31,915 --> 00:03:36,578
For example, run the status check with ready, one of its allowed labels.

60
00:03:36,578 --> 00:03:38,651
It is accepted, as status ready.

61
00:03:38,651 --> 00:03:41,954
Our scope statement names the one label we checked,

62
00:03:41,954 --> 00:03:44,674
and leaves the other labels outside scope.

63
00:03:45,714 --> 00:03:47,793
Write every row in the same shape.

64
00:03:47,793 --> 00:03:49,749
The finding and its disposition.

65
00:03:49,749 --> 00:03:50,727
The requirement.

66
00:03:50,727 --> 00:03:52,928
The evidence command and its output.

67
00:03:52,928 --> 00:03:55,617
The observed effect and the protected state.

68
00:03:55,964 --> 00:04:00,612
For an undetermined row, the missing input, or why it cannot be decided.

69
00:04:00,612 --> 00:04:04,486
And for every row, the scope, and the question that remains.

70
00:04:04,831 --> 00:04:07,178
The own check is one of two kinds.

71
00:04:07,178 --> 00:04:08,076
A new defect:

72
00:04:08,076 --> 00:04:13,324
a check outside the recorded inputs whose observation demonstrates a defect.

73
00:04:13,324 --> 00:04:15,879
Or a scope check: no defect observed,

74
00:04:15,879 --> 00:04:19,262
and a sentence naming the range and its boundary.

75
00:04:20,297 --> 00:04:22,543
Then hand the record to the verifier.

76
00:04:22,543 --> 00:04:26,610
It reruns every named check, checks the exact reproducible command,

77
00:04:26,610 --> 00:04:30,191
and derives the supported disposition from the observation,

78
00:04:30,191 --> 00:04:32,255
not from a label in the recording.

79
00:04:32,597 --> 00:04:36,376
We filled a record in a scratch copy: the three dispositions,

80
00:04:36,376 --> 00:04:38,668
with the export path as a new defect.

81
00:04:38,668 --> 00:04:40,527
The verifier reports verified.

82
00:04:40,864 --> 00:04:45,679
Then, as the workshop suggests, mark the false positive confirmed once.

83
00:04:45,679 --> 00:04:50,291
Rejected: the disposition is not supported by the runnable evidence.

84
00:04:50,630 --> 00:04:54,780
Put a hand trace where the command belongs, and it is rejected again.

85
00:04:54,780 --> 00:04:57,968
The command is not the reproducible launcher command.

86
00:04:58,314 --> 00:05:02,863
It also rejects an item with no evidence, an empty undetermined reason,

87
00:05:02,863 --> 00:05:05,683
a changed argument, and a missing own check.

88
00:05:05,683 --> 00:05:07,413
And it never calls a model.

89
00:05:07,413 --> 00:05:10,040
Model output never enters a scoring path.

90
00:05:11,078 --> 00:05:12,582
M3 is individual work,

91
00:05:12,582 --> 00:05:17,296
and it runs the same sequence on your own frozen repository snapshot.

92
00:05:17,296 --> 00:05:21,601
The teaching team runs one model review and keeps the original.

93
00:05:21,601 --> 00:05:24,198
You submit verification evidence only.

94
00:05:24,545 --> 00:05:29,860
Use only the frozen project snapshot and the minimum de-identified evidence.

95
00:05:29,860 --> 00:05:34,755
Never include participant material, private credentials, session logs,

96
00:05:34,755 --> 00:05:36,643
or unrelated personal data.

97
00:05:36,978 --> 00:05:41,237
And when evidence conflicts, it goes to the human integrity process.

98
00:05:41,237 --> 00:05:45,245
An automatic authorship detector does not decide responsibility.

99
00:05:46,278 --> 00:05:50,655
Three meanings, each tied to a runnable observation on this snapshot.

100
00:05:50,994 --> 00:05:55,671
And a successful command supports only the path and revision it exercised.

101
00:05:55,671 --> 00:06:00,410
Evidence from a repaired revision cannot close a finding on the frozen one.

102
00:06:00,744 --> 00:06:04,259
So a test for the defect should fail before any repair.

103
00:06:04,259 --> 00:06:09,115
A test that passes after a repair cannot prove the frozen defect was absent.

104
00:06:10,161 --> 00:06:14,747
So the observation decides the disposition, not the wording of the claim.

105
00:06:15,094 --> 00:06:16,255
One question to try.

106
00:06:16,255 --> 00:06:20,145
On your own frozen snapshot, which path did the review not mention,

107
00:06:20,145 --> 00:06:22,002
and what command would check it?

episodes.title: Keep the layers apart
episodes.decision: a finding has three layers: what was observed, what is hypothesised and what is changed. Keep them in separate fields, and make each one stronger in its own way. Generate a bounded change, predict the evidence before accepting it, and let each check answer only its own question: a green unit test cannot certify a label, and an old session cannot show that a new label is understandable. Then name the decision with one of four words in one record, and accept an iteration only for the scope that was checked. The same separation carries into a team's platform (each shared piece concentrates authority) and into an eight-minute demo (need, finding, change, verification, decision, limit).

subtitles.en:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,493
Here is a course-authored interface.

2
00:00:02,493 --> 00:00:06,301
Its visible controls are Overview, Options and Refresh.

3
00:00:06,301 --> 00:00:10,593
Inside Options, a State filter offers All, Failed and Running.

4
00:00:10,593 --> 00:00:15,232
The task is to find the most recent failed build in pipeline Alpha.

5
00:00:15,567 --> 00:00:19,708
The supplied record says the user opens Overview, then returns.

6
00:00:19,708 --> 00:00:23,981
They select Refresh twice, and ask where failed builds are shown.

7
00:00:23,981 --> 00:00:25,691
The task is not completed.

8
00:00:26,033 --> 00:00:29,102
Yet the query returns the correct failed records.

9
00:00:29,102 --> 00:00:33,673
So behavior correctness and locating the control are different questions.

10
00:00:34,017 --> 00:00:36,717
Before going on, write an observation,

11
00:00:36,717 --> 00:00:40,128
a hypothesis and a candidate change of your own.

12
00:00:40,128 --> 00:00:45,743
The record contains no real participant, timestamp or population-level finding.

13
00:00:46,783 --> 00:00:49,512
The observation is what the record shows.

14
00:00:49,512 --> 00:00:54,968
"Options may not communicate status filtering" is an interpretation: a hypothesis.

15
00:00:55,317 --> 00:00:59,756
Write them in separate fields before asking an assistant for a patch.

16
00:00:59,756 --> 00:01:03,681
If they share one sentence, split them before implementation.

17
00:01:03,681 --> 00:01:07,542
And this is a reasoning aid, not a claim about a population.

18
00:01:08,583 --> 00:01:11,301
Each layer gets stronger in its own way.

19
00:01:11,301 --> 00:01:17,755
The observation is stronger when the same action is recorded on the affected revision and task.

20
00:01:18,100 --> 00:01:24,892
The hypothesis is stronger when a neutral task can tell locating the control apart from query correctness.

21
00:01:25,233 --> 00:01:30,597
And the change is stronger when a diff and an explicit acceptance check show the intended scope.

22
00:01:31,633 --> 00:01:37,183
Exposing Status: All is one plausible change to test, not a proven solution.

23
00:01:37,516 --> 00:01:40,484
Generation is the request for a bounded patch.

24
00:01:40,484 --> 00:01:45,515
Add the control to the existing Options path, and preserve the query contract,

25
00:01:45,515 --> 00:01:48,999
result order, permission check and keyboard operation.

26
00:01:49,333 --> 00:01:52,697
If the change is larger than the hypothesis, narrow it,

27
00:01:52,697 --> 00:01:55,266
or record why a product owner must decide.

28
00:01:55,600 --> 00:01:59,298
An assistant may propose code within the assignment's rules.

29
00:01:59,298 --> 00:02:03,367
You own the discovery records, and the interpretation of evidence.

30
00:02:04,416 --> 00:02:07,409
Before accepting a patch, predict the evidence.

31
00:02:07,409 --> 00:02:11,039
The unchanged query check still returns the same records.

32
00:02:11,039 --> 00:02:14,095
The integration check sends the selected status.

33
00:02:14,095 --> 00:02:17,343
The keyboard check reaches and changes the control.

34
00:02:17,343 --> 00:02:23,329
And a new authorized task observation records whether the control can be found without a hint.

35
00:02:23,666 --> 00:02:28,589
Then run each check on the revision being discussed, and record the observed result.

36
00:02:29,633 --> 00:02:32,388
A green unit test cannot certify a label.

37
00:02:32,388 --> 00:02:37,899
And a successful task observation cannot certify an unchanged permission boundary.

38
00:02:38,233 --> 00:02:42,956
The old session cannot show that the new label is understandable, either.

39
00:02:42,956 --> 00:02:45,802
Repeat the neutral task on the new revision.

40
00:02:46,149 --> 00:02:50,172
Do it under the actual consent or equivalence arrangement.

41
00:02:50,172 --> 00:02:53,987
And keep minimal de-identified observations, not names,

42
00:02:53,987 --> 00:02:56,761
raw media or unrelated personal details.

43
00:02:57,799 --> 00:03:02,958
Finding A reproduces an archived owner's edit, contrary to the agreed policy.

44
00:03:02,958 --> 00:03:07,714
Repair it, and verify the reproducer plus the allowed-role regressions.

45
00:03:08,049 --> 00:03:12,036
Finding B asks that all unknown statuses become failed.

46
00:03:12,036 --> 00:03:16,240
Under the current contract, that is a new product meaning.

47
00:03:16,240 --> 00:03:21,097
A reasoned response can decline it, citing the unknown-status rule,

48
00:03:21,097 --> 00:03:23,054
or seek a product decision.

49
00:03:23,054 --> 00:03:27,403
Reviewer identity is not a reason to dismiss either finding.

50
00:03:28,449 --> 00:03:31,149
Use the four disposition words consistently.

51
00:03:31,149 --> 00:03:35,444
Repair, when the demonstrated behavior violates an agreed requirement,

52
00:03:35,444 --> 00:03:39,003
and the reproducer plus relevant regressions can be rerun.

53
00:03:39,349 --> 00:03:42,307
Investigate, when the signal is incomplete,

54
00:03:42,307 --> 00:03:46,710
and a named observation or check is needed before changing code.

55
00:03:47,049 --> 00:03:50,999
Disagree, when the request changes the current product meaning,

56
00:03:50,999 --> 00:03:54,573
and the record explains the contract and its consequence.

57
00:03:54,916 --> 00:03:58,399
Defer, when the question is real but outside this iteration,

58
00:03:58,399 --> 00:04:01,011
with an owner and a trigger for reopening it.

59
00:04:01,349 --> 00:04:05,730
Write the decision in one existing record: the finding and revision,

60
00:04:05,730 --> 00:04:09,596
the requirement, the changed scope, the actual verification,

61
00:04:09,596 --> 00:04:12,238
and the remaining question and its owner.

62
00:04:12,238 --> 00:04:14,557
A label such as fixed, or won't fix,

63
00:04:14,557 --> 00:04:17,650
alone does not explain the engineering judgment.

64
00:04:18,699 --> 00:04:23,444
If the current iteration passes the affected behavior and keyboard checks,

65
00:04:23,444 --> 00:04:28,253
and an authorized new session completes the task without a navigation hint,

66
00:04:28,253 --> 00:04:31,075
accept the iteration for that checked scope.

67
00:04:31,415 --> 00:04:34,620
Do not claim that all users will now succeed.

68
00:04:35,665 --> 00:04:40,800
What works for one developer needs shared infrastructure when a whole team adopts it.

69
00:04:40,800 --> 00:04:41,888
Four pieces recur.

70
00:04:42,232 --> 00:04:47,394
A tool portal gives agents one permissioned entry point to the team's tools,

71
00:04:47,394 --> 00:04:50,519
so access is granted and revoked in one place.

72
00:04:50,519 --> 00:04:54,322
A model gateway sits between agents and model providers,

73
00:04:54,322 --> 00:04:59,960
and holds what individuals should not: keys, budgets, rate limits and request logs.

74
00:05:00,298 --> 00:05:04,954
Routing sends a task to the cheapest model that passes your evaluator,

75
00:05:04,954 --> 00:05:07,482
and escalates only when a check fails.

76
00:05:07,482 --> 00:05:10,009
That is why the evaluator comes first.

77
00:05:10,009 --> 00:05:13,468
Cost accounting counts what an accepted change cost,

78
00:05:13,468 --> 00:05:16,261
including failed attempts and review time,

79
00:05:16,261 --> 00:05:20,651
because cost per token rewards cheap output that nobody can merge.

80
00:05:20,998 --> 00:05:23,477
This course operates none of these.

81
00:05:23,477 --> 00:05:27,018
Recognize them, say which problem each one solves,

82
00:05:27,018 --> 00:05:32,399
and notice that each one concentrates authority, so it needs boundary tests.

83
00:05:33,448 --> 00:05:36,332
The team demo is a communication exercise.

84
00:05:36,332 --> 00:05:41,343
It is not a second test, and not a substitute for the individual defense.

85
00:05:41,682 --> 00:05:44,988
Give it six moves, each with a visible artifact.

86
00:05:44,988 --> 00:05:49,052
Need, one minute: the user task and the agreed requirement.

87
00:05:49,052 --> 00:05:54,424
Finding, one minute: one observation, with the hypothesis labelled separately.

88
00:05:54,424 --> 00:05:59,108
Change, two minutes: the smallest change, and what stayed unchanged.

89
00:05:59,448 --> 00:06:04,287
Verification, two minutes: the expected result before the output.

90
00:06:04,287 --> 00:06:05,850
Decision, one minute.

91
00:06:05,850 --> 00:06:12,103
And limit, one minute: what this evidence supports, and what still needs a new test.

92
00:06:12,448 --> 00:06:18,236
Rehearse with a course-authored preview, or the team's approved, de-identified work.

93
00:06:18,236 --> 00:06:21,819
Do not paste participant identities, raw recordings,

94
00:06:21,819 --> 00:06:25,126
private code or model transcripts into the deck.

95
00:06:26,164 --> 00:06:30,202
So keep the observation, the hypothesis and the change apart,

96
00:06:30,202 --> 00:06:33,049
and let each check answer its own question.

97
00:06:33,397 --> 00:06:34,605
One question to try.

98
00:06:34,605 --> 00:06:37,505
What would you check if the label changed again?

99
00:06:37,505 --> 00:06:41,975
Name the new input, the expected effect, and the decision that would move.

100
00:06:41,975 --> 00:06:46,807
If the existing test cannot see the changed condition, name the different check.

episodes.title: Has it ever failed?
episodes.decision: claim only the scope you checked, and trust a check only once you have seen it fail. The practice packet's code predicts that a guest is denied, but the evidence matrix never observed a guest, so acceptance extends only to cases that were checked. Our scratch run of Snapshot B's lines shows the guest cases behaving as predicted, and a deliberately broken variant shows the check can fail; it still supports only those lines, not the request and stored title. A changed condition in rehearsal (a role policy, an output format, a timeout) needs its own evidence, and a demo keeps its failures. The same rule decides the software-factory claim stage by stage: a stage may run unattended only with a check seen to fail on a bad input and pass on a good one, and a stop path someone has exercised.

subtitles.en:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,456
The agreed policy permits an edit exactly when two things hold.

2
00:00:04,456 --> 00:00:07,709
Owner or staff is true, and archived is false.

3
00:00:07,709 --> 00:00:10,751
A guest means both role booleans are false.

4
00:00:11,100 --> 00:00:15,673
Snapshot B computes allowed as owner or staff, and not archived.

5
00:00:15,673 --> 00:00:18,530
If allowed, it sets the requested title.

6
00:00:18,867 --> 00:00:23,564
The supplied evidence matrix covers an active owner and active staff,

7
00:00:23,564 --> 00:00:28,602
both allowed with the new title, and an archived owner and archived staff,

8
00:00:28,602 --> 00:00:30,712
both denied with the old title.

9
00:00:30,712 --> 00:00:32,278
Guest cases are absent.

10
00:00:32,278 --> 00:00:36,839
Predict an active guest's decision and final title before going on.

11
00:00:37,883 --> 00:00:40,209
So what happens to an active guest?

12
00:00:40,209 --> 00:00:43,400
The code predicts denial and an unchanged title.

13
00:00:43,400 --> 00:00:46,324
But the provided matrix has not observed it.

14
00:00:46,667 --> 00:00:48,171
State that distinction,

15
00:00:48,171 --> 00:00:52,748
and propose the guest request with both response and state assertions.

16
00:00:52,748 --> 00:00:58,044
If those checks then complete on B, acceptance can extend to those checked cases.

17
00:00:58,383 --> 00:01:03,155
A phrase such as "all permission boundaries are safe" would exceed this packet.

18
00:01:04,200 --> 00:01:07,241
Before that real check, a quick one of our own.

19
00:01:07,241 --> 00:01:10,995
We wrapped Snapshot B's three lines in a scratch function,

20
00:01:10,995 --> 00:01:14,231
and ran it for an active guest with the old title.

21
00:01:14,566 --> 00:01:17,576
It denies the edit, and the title stays Old.

22
00:01:17,576 --> 00:01:22,844
The archived guest gets the same, and the four matrix cases match the record.

23
00:01:23,183 --> 00:01:25,684
Would this check notice a bad change?

24
00:01:25,684 --> 00:01:29,266
We broke the rule on purpose, dropping the role test.

25
00:01:29,266 --> 00:01:33,254
Now the active guest is allowed, and the title becomes New.

26
00:01:33,254 --> 00:01:36,093
The check fails, so it can see that fault.

27
00:01:36,433 --> 00:01:39,927
This run supports only these cases on B's three lines.

28
00:01:39,927 --> 00:01:44,328
The response and the stored title still need the real guest request.

29
00:01:45,366 --> 00:01:49,122
A concise account links a user need to a source change,

30
00:01:49,122 --> 00:01:51,717
a discriminating check and a revision.

31
00:01:52,066 --> 00:01:54,247
Archived content needs protection.

32
00:01:54,247 --> 00:01:56,556
The old owner term bypassed archive.

33
00:01:56,556 --> 00:01:59,570
The new grouping applies archive to both roles.

34
00:01:59,570 --> 00:02:03,932
And the archived-owner regression checks denial and unchanged state.

35
00:02:04,266 --> 00:02:07,958
A complete spoken explanation does not create missing evidence.

36
00:02:09,000 --> 00:02:13,917
When you rehearse, a peer changes one condition, and you answer it yourself.

37
00:02:13,917 --> 00:02:19,029
Staff may now edit archived builds, but owners who are not staff still may not.

38
00:02:19,029 --> 00:02:22,911
A changed role policy needs its own authorization and cases,

39
00:02:22,911 --> 00:02:25,823
not a silent rewrite of the old expectations.

40
00:02:26,166 --> 00:02:29,070
The output changes from yes or no to JSON.

41
00:02:29,070 --> 00:02:33,286
That needs a new accepted contract and matching scorer tests.

42
00:02:33,286 --> 00:02:36,673
A prior pass remains evidence for the old format.

43
00:02:37,016 --> 00:02:40,683
A timeout occurs before stored state is inspected.

44
00:02:40,683 --> 00:02:44,643
It can mean no commit, or a lost reply after a commit.

45
00:02:44,643 --> 00:02:48,383
Inspect the operation key and the persisted effect.

46
00:02:49,416 --> 00:02:53,704
In the demonstration, show one user task, its visible behavior,

47
00:02:53,704 --> 00:02:55,814
and the check that supports it.

48
00:02:55,814 --> 00:03:01,259
Identify the actual revision, and explain a decision and the limit that remains.

49
00:03:01,600 --> 00:03:05,862
If the live path fails, keep that result and state the next observation.

50
00:03:05,862 --> 00:03:09,710
Use a labelled recording only if the announced format permits it,

51
00:03:09,710 --> 00:03:12,374
and never relabel an older result as current.

52
00:03:12,716 --> 00:03:19,692
And a later task taking less time than an earlier one does not isolate an agent's productivity effect.

53
00:03:19,692 --> 00:03:23,316
Difficulty, familiarity and team practice may differ.

54
00:03:24,350 --> 00:03:28,095
A software factory organizes requirements, generation,

55
00:03:28,095 --> 00:03:32,464
verification and delivery into a repeatable production process.

56
00:03:32,464 --> 00:03:37,458
The stronger claim is that its stages could run with little human input.

57
00:03:37,458 --> 00:03:40,232
Treat that as a claim, not a conclusion.

58
00:03:40,566 --> 00:03:45,549
Test it on the one pipeline you know in detail: your own ci-dashboard work.

59
00:03:45,549 --> 00:03:50,599
Split it into stages, and for each one, ask whether it could run unattended,

60
00:03:50,599 --> 00:03:53,256
and what evidence would be needed first.

61
00:03:53,600 --> 00:03:57,579
For the test stage, the tests must fail on meaningful faults,

62
00:03:57,579 --> 00:04:00,449
not only on the cases they were written for.

63
00:04:00,449 --> 00:04:05,080
For the evaluate stage, the scorer has been challenged and still holds,

64
00:04:05,080 --> 00:04:07,625
and Unknown is never counted as a pass.

65
00:04:08,666 --> 00:04:13,937
A synthetic team proposes letting an agent merge two kinds of change unattended.

66
00:04:14,283 --> 00:04:19,093
For dependency updates, tests and the evaluator rerun on every update,

67
00:04:19,093 --> 00:04:24,316
and a deliberately broken update failed both before the team relied on them.

68
00:04:24,316 --> 00:04:27,752
The recovery drill also rolled back a bad version.

69
00:04:27,752 --> 00:04:33,043
That is a candidate for unattended merge, with a stop rule: any failed check,

70
00:04:33,043 --> 00:04:37,166
refused cap or rollback stops the agent and pages the owner.

71
00:04:37,500 --> 00:04:40,292
For the permission rule, the tests pass,

72
00:04:40,292 --> 00:04:44,969
but an audit found an archived-owner bypass those tests had missed.

73
00:04:44,969 --> 00:04:50,693
Not yet: a person reviews these changes until a regression for that bypass exists,

74
00:04:50,693 --> 00:04:53,905
and has been seen to fail on the pre-fix code.

75
00:04:54,250 --> 00:04:56,975
So the useful outcome is a bounded claim:

76
00:04:56,975 --> 00:05:00,764
unattended for dependency updates under these stop rules,

77
00:05:00,764 --> 00:05:03,357
and reviewed for authorization changes.

78
00:05:03,357 --> 00:05:06,614
It is not a yes or no about factories in general.

79
00:05:07,649 --> 00:05:13,605
A check that has never been seen to fail is not yet evidence that it would stop a bad change.

80
00:05:13,949 --> 00:05:20,924
So a stage you mark unattended needs a check you have seen fail on a bad input and pass on a good one,

81
00:05:20,924 --> 00:05:23,864
and a stop path that someone has exercised.

82
00:05:23,864 --> 00:05:29,402
A stage supported only by passing runs is not yet, however many passes there are.

83
00:05:30,449 --> 00:05:35,908
Before an agent runs unattended, answer three questions with something you can test.

84
00:05:35,908 --> 00:05:36,948
Who can stop it?

85
00:05:36,948 --> 00:05:37,923
A named person,

86
00:05:37,923 --> 00:05:42,862
with a stop that works without a deploy and without the agent's cooperation.

87
00:05:42,862 --> 00:05:44,097
What may it change?

88
00:05:44,097 --> 00:05:48,581
Permitted actions and paths, granted in one place, with per-run caps.

89
00:05:48,581 --> 00:05:49,816
How is it observed?

90
00:05:49,816 --> 00:05:53,391
A minimal record of what it read, proposed and changed,

91
00:05:53,391 --> 00:05:55,666
and an alert when a cap refuses it.

92
00:05:56,015 --> 00:06:01,928
Then test the stop: stop the agent midway, and check that no partial effect remains.

93
00:06:01,928 --> 00:06:06,080
That is the same idempotency question as a retried request.

94
00:06:06,080 --> 00:06:09,670
And rerun the frozen evaluator cases on a schedule,

95
00:06:09,670 --> 00:06:15,160
because a hosted model's name does not guarantee unchanged behavior over time.

96
00:06:15,499 --> 00:06:19,468
If you cannot answer one of these for a stage of your pipeline,

97
00:06:19,468 --> 00:06:21,106
that stage needs a person.

98
00:06:22,149 --> 00:06:24,132
So claim only the scope you checked,

99
00:06:24,132 --> 00:06:27,547
and count a check as evidence only once you have seen it fail.

100
00:06:27,882 --> 00:06:29,119
One question to try.

101
00:06:29,119 --> 00:06:32,581
Which observation changed one of your project decisions?

102
00:06:32,581 --> 00:06:35,858
Then name a new input that would make you revisit it.
